subject: TIA handshake: MarketplaceX onboarding — routing & evidence ask
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@marketplacex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TIA handshake: MarketplaceX onboarding — routing & evidence ask

Hi Alice — great to meet you via the intro last week. We're excited to get MarketplaceX onto Redwood for the seller analytics and recommendations use-case. Before we kick off the Dedicated evaluation and formal onboarding, legal/security asked for a short TIA-style handshake so we can scope any cross-border safeguards up front.

Could you please share the following items by EOD next Tuesday (6/29) if possible? If not, let us know a realistic ETA. We want to avoid scope creep when timelining Dedicated capacity and the UK addendum.

1) A simple flow diagram (PNG/PDF) showing where PII/customer identifiers originate, which subsystems process it (payment, seller profiles, analytics), and any third-party subprocessors involved for each hop.
2) A current subprocessor list (CSV) with country of processing and whether they persist logs.
3) Confirmation on payment routing: which payments hit US-based processors versus EU-only processors (Stripe/others). If you have a matrix by country that helps.
4) Retention policy for logs and transaction identifiers (how long do seller IDs and raw logs persist).
5) Any SOC 2 / ISO/attestation dates we can rely on for the next 12 months.

Attachments: I dropped a quick example evidence checklist (marketplacex-evidence-template.docx) to the shared Drive link below — feel free to edit and return.

Next steps from our side: Laura will scope the TIA and draft a proposed routing fallback (EU->UK->US order) for review, and Kim will vet subprocessor encryption/egress controls. I’ll coordinate the mutual action plan and timeline.

Thanks — simple answers to the items above will let us keep the DTA/TIA narrow and avoid a protracted request cycle.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments (referenced): marketplacex-evidence-template.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TIA handshake: MarketplaceX onboarding — routing & evidence ask

Marissa — thanks, noted. Quick internal plan:

- I will own the TIA scoping doc and produce a 1-page routing summary (EU vs UK vs US) by Mon 6/28 EOD.
- Kim will review subprocessor encryption-at-rest and egress restrictions and flag any blockers (ETA Tue 6/29).
- Jonas will validate the model-serving footprints (where inference happens) and whether KV cache data touches EU hosts.

Suggested mutual action plan to propose to MarketplaceX:
- Day 0 (today): Handshake + list of evidence we need (Marissa's email).
- Day 2 (6/29): MarketplaceX returns flow diagram + subprocessor CSV.
- Day 4 (7/01): Redwood provides proposed TIA scope + UK addendum checklist + redlineable SCCs draft.
- Day 8 (7/05): Finalize routing policy; identify any required contractual exceptions.

I'll draft the short TIA scope now and share in Drive.

Laura
Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TIA handshake: MarketplaceX onboarding — routing & evidence ask

Hi Marissa/Laura/Kim — thanks for the clear list. Happy to share what's available today and to fill gaps quickly. Quick answers inline: 

1) Flow diagram: attached (mx-payment-flow.png) — shows seller webhook -> payments -> analytics pipeline -> reporting.
2) Subprocessors: attached CSV (marketplacex-subprocessors.csv). EU subprocessors include two EU-based analytics vendors and a CDN; Stripe (payments) is the primary processor and routing is US by default for reconciliation, but we can route EU-resident customers through our EU Stripe instance (configurable per account).
3) Payment processors: Stripe (primary, US/Global), Adyen (EU for selected merchants), Klarna (EU in Nordics).
4) Retention: Transaction logs and raw webhook payloads retained 180 days by default; hashed identifiers retained for 540 days. We can do a 90-day retention for EU-only merchant accounts with a contract clause.
5) Attestations: We have SOC 2 Type II (last report: 2026-11) and ISO 27001 (certificate: 2025-05).

Links and attachments: I've uploaded the flow PNG and the subprocessors CSV to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB...marketplacex-evidence

Next: ops@marketplacex.com (cc'd) can share a sample merchant onboarding doc and the country-matrix by EOD Tue. If you want, we can run a short 30-min call Tue to review the routing exceptions and UK addendum expectations.

Best,
Alice Turner
Head of Platform Ops — MarketplaceX
alice.turner@marketplacex.com

Attachments: mx-payment-flow.png, marketplacex-subprocessors.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@marketplacex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TIA handshake: MarketplaceX onboarding — routing & evidence ask

Alice — thanks, this is great and helps a lot. Quick follow-ups so we can lock the TIA scope: 

- Can you also provide a sample merchant onboarding sheet highlighting the fields that carry seller identifiers and any country-of-residence flags (ops mentioned they'd share this).
- For the EU Stripe instance: can ops confirm whether transaction-level metadata (IP address, payer email) is stored outside the EU for reconciliation? If yes, we will need to scope a UK Addendum carve-out for UK resident sellers and an explicit TIA mapping for EU-resident seller flows.
- Please confirm whether any subprocessor persists full webhook payloads beyond the 180-day default; if so, which processors and where geographically.

Action items we’ll take on:
- Laura: draft a two-page TIA scope that calls out EU-only merchant routing + UK addendum gating criteria.
- Kim: generate a short checklist for encryption/egress controls for each listed subprocessor.
- Jonas: check inference KV cache footprint for seller identifiers and whether we need to isolate EU-only keys.

If Ops can do a 30-min sync, we propose Tue 6/29 15:00 UTC / 08:00 PT. If that doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks again — once we have the sample merchant file and confirmation on Stripe metadata, we can keep the TIA narrow and avoid a full DPA rework.

Marissa
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

We need a quick confirmation on whether Redwood's inference KV cache would ever hold raw seller identifiers for analytic enrichment of merchant accounts that are EU-resident. If yes, we must propose an isolation plan (EU-only keyspace) in the TIA.

Please see attachments (mx-payment-flow.png, marketplacex-subprocessors.csv). Action items:
- Infra: confirm KV cache residency (EU-hosted shards?) and whether we can pin EU-only keys for a customer-scoped model.
- Security: review subprocessors CSV and highlight any vendors that do not support customer-managed encryption keys.
- Legal/Privacy: Laura/Marissa will finalize gating contract language for UK Addendum carve-outs.
